Diego R: @channel Heads-up: planned maintenance + capacity rebalance for H200 reserved pools in eu-west-1. This will create a temporary surge window where we route eligible workloads to alternate H200 zones and A10G reserved as a secondary fallback. Maintenance window: 2025-10-14 22:00 -> 2025-10-15 04:00 UTC.
Nia H: What triggers the rebalance vs normal maintenance?
Diego R: Nia H: it's two-part: (1) firmware upgrade we must apply to 3 racks, (2) proactive hot-shift to reduce cross-AZ tail latency we've observed under heavy cache pressure. To avoid customer impact we'll pre-fill alternate pools and route non-pinned, non-urgent traffic there during the window.
SRE-Oncall: What's the expected capacity delta per zone?
Diego R: Expect ~18-22% reduction in primary AZ capacity during the 6h window; alternate AZs will accept up to +25% aggregated temporary allocations. We'll throttle if tail latency regresses.
EngInfra: ops helper to preview affected instances:
```
# preview instances that will be candidates for auto-shift
redwoodctl instances list --filter "region=eu-west-1 AND gpu=h200_reserved AND status=running" --fields id,customer_id,pinned_model,route_bucket | grep -v test-
```
EngInfra: also added an internal tag `maintenance.candidate-20251014` to mark candidates.
OpsBot: [automated] Maintenance reminders created: 72h/24h/1h before window. Live status updates will be posted to #eng-oncall during the window.
Asha P: Any console UX changes customers will see?
Diego R: Yes: console banner for affected customers with an option: "Opt-out of auto-shift" (will keep jobs pinned but may be queued), or "Allow auto-shift to alternate H200 zones" (recommended). We'll send targeted emails to routes with urgent bucket or pinned models.
CustomerSuccess: We'll prepare email templates and an FAQ. Also will surface a link to a quick-check tool so customers can verify compatibility.
Billing: Any billing implications for shifted workloads?
Billing: No SKU change when we shift between H200 reserved zones. If we fallback to A10G reserved for compatibility mismatches, billing will include a `fallback_a10g_adjustment` line item; customers on committed contracts will be contacted before any A10G fallback is applied.
SRE-Oncall: alerts we should watch?
Diego R: New alerts for the window: `dedicated.h200.maintenance.rebalance` (informational during window), `dedicated.h200.maintenance.latency_regress` (fires if p99 increases >25% from baseline for 10m), `dedicated.h200.maintenance.fallback_count` (tracks fallbacks to A10G >0.5% thresh). We'll enable pagers for the first 2h.
EngInfra: Quick operator script to force-remove maintenance tag if needed:
```
redwoodctl instances tag --remove maintenance.candidate-20251014 --filter "customer_id=acct_1234"
```
Nia H: How do we handle long-running jobs that started on affected racks?
Diego R: Long-running pinned jobs will be left alone. For batch jobs with no pin and with flexible SLA, we will attempt a graceful handoff at job checkpoint boundaries. We'll post detailed migration semantics in the runbook.
Asha P: Can we run a small simulation before the window?
Diego R: Yes  dry-run in staging next Wed 2025-10-08 10:00 UTC. We'll simulate 10% of traffic and validate fallback metrics. Invite to follow.
CustomerSuccess: We'll include the dry-run summary link in customer comms so folks can decide opt-in.
Billing: Action: prepare note on `fallback_a10g_adjustment` and add to the billing FAQ (due 2025-10-10).
EngInfra: Action: publish runbook + scripts (EOD 2025-10-09), SRE: enable alerts & dashboards (EOD 2025-10-10), Support & CS: send targeted emails (2025-10-11), Ops: monitor during window and post debrief.
Diego R: Thanks team. Post any blockers here or DM me. We'll update the internal doc: <https://go.redwood.ai/internal/dedicated/h200-eu-maintenance-rebalance>. :white_check_mark:
